title: 2006 HMMT February Guts Problem 12
statement: For each positive integer \(n\) let \(S_{n}\) denote the set \(\{1,2,3, \ldots, n\}\). Compute the number of triples of subsets \(A, B, C\) of \(S_{2006}\) (not necessarily nonempty or proper) such that \(A\) is a subset of \(B\) and \(S_{2006}-A\) is a subset of \(C\).

solutions.text:
Let \(A_{o}, B_{o}, C_{o}\) be sets satisfying the said conditions. Note that \(1 \in A_{o}\) implies that \(1 \in B_{o}\) and \(1 \notin S_{2006}-A_{o}\) so that 1 may or may not be in \(C_{o}\). Also,
\(1 \notin A_{o}\) implies that \(1 \in S_{2006}-A_{o} \subset C_{o}\) while 1 may or may not be in \(B_{o}\). Thus there are four possibilities for the distribution of 1 , and since the same argument holds independently for \(2,3, \ldots, 2006\), the answer is \(4^{2006}\) or \(2^{4012}\).
